newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil blue chips soar, market ends up 3.15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil blue chips soar, market ends up 3.15 pct.

text.p: Brazilian stocks surged to close a strong 3.15 percent higher Thursday led by soaring blue chips amid heavy and volatile options-related trade, brokers said.
"There's a lot of money coming into the market," a local trader told Reuters. "We're pretty close to options expiration."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index ended at 11,852 points, led by rising blue chips Eletrobras, Petrobras and Telebras in hefty trade totalling 1.047 billion reais ($969 million).

Brokers said investors went on a buying spree late in the session, snapping up benchmark Telebras ahead of options settlements next Monday and accelerating an ongoing trend of diversifying from telecoms into other sectors.
"People are diversifying into eletricals and Petrobras," one dealer said. "This was really big today and I think it's because we're near the expirations."
The market also was aided by strong rises on Wall Street and declines in U.S. interest rates, traders said.
Buying was concentrated in blue chips, but Telebras' volume dropped below 50 percent of total trade for the first time in weeks.
Bellwether Telebras preferred, boosted by options holders with long positions, climbed 3.19 percent to end at 152.20 reais, while its common rose 2.19 percent to end at 139.70 reais.
Its Sao Paulo unit Telesp also rose amid the volatile pre-options buying, closing 4.14 percent higher at 352 reais.

But Petrobras' preferred led the blue-chip rally, rising 5.72 percent to end at 296 reais followed by state power holding Eletrobras' preferred B share, which gained 4.87 percent to close at 560 reais.
The rise in Eletrobras helped boost the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index, which jumped 4.28 percent to close at 3,247 points.
But other power shares also rose strongly, led by Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) preferred, which surged 7.01 percent on a wave of buying.
CPFL, considered the jewel of the Sao Paulo state's electrical sector, is expected to be privatized in October.
Brokers said the options-related fluctuations made it hard to predict Friday's open and urged caution as both the local and New York bourses appear poised for a wave of profit-taking.
"This is an options war and all caution is little ahead of expiration," one trader said. "Tomorrow we could go down."
